rule: Crop the single colour-1 panel. It carries three single-cell corner markers (cells diagonally inside three panel corners) and an interior shape. Apply the unique rotation or reflection that puts each marker in the same relative corner as the loose same-coloured dot outside the panel. The dots lie on three corners of an axis-aligned rectangle.
scope: Crop the colour-1 panel and choose the unique dihedral transform whose three distinct inset corner markers match the pairwise row/column ordering of three external dots. Feasible panel dimensions and transform are selected analytically before shape sampling. Default dot spacing matches transformed marker spacing; explicit spacing/straddling extensions remain supported. Border-connected panel 1 s must be the unique largest single-colour 4-component. All four canonical pairs reconstruct exactly.

authored_scope: Supported: panel sides 5..26. They are sampled jointly with the transform and layout in a bounded retry loop, usually 7..14 and sometimes up to 22 as a synthetic extension. Panel area must be at most 448. Any missing corner, distinct marker and shape colours in 2..9, random-walk shapes with optional stray cells, all 7 non-identity transforms by default (identity only on request), canvases up to 30x30, and dots on any side of the panel with span equal to the output marker spacing. Explicit-only synthetic extensions: dot_box spans that differ from the marker spacing, and straddling layouts. Not supported: other background or panel colours, more than one panel, markers off the diagonal-inside-corner cells, panels or dots touching the canvas edge.
authored_constraints: Exactly three distinct marker colours in 2..9 at three of (1,1), (1,w-2), (h-2,1), (h-2,w-2); the shape colour is distinct from them and from 0 and 1.
Shape cells lie in rows 2..h-3 and cols 2..w-3, so they never overwrite the panel border ring or a marker. Diagonal contact with a marker is allowed, as in train pair 3.
Colour-1 cells outnumber shape cells inside the panel.
The three dots sit on corners of an axis-aligned rectangle with both spans >= 2, outside the panel and its 1-cell halo, and within the 1-cell canvas margin.
Each dot's corner equals the corresponding marker's corner in the output. With three corners of a rectangle, exactly one of the 8 dihedral transforms matches.
Background 0 is the strict majority colour of the input.
All integer controls reject bools, floats and out-of-range values with ValueError.
